correctness.rationale: For b,n>=3, the full proof first reconstructs the exact-distance-two criterion and then classifies sections by the third coordinate. With two active layers vertical pairs are impossible; equal binary coordinates force coincident singleton y-supports and opposite binary coordinates force disjoint y-supports. The five exhaustive occupancy cases yield the displayed polynomial; only the one-layer-versus-multilayer opposite-binary case reaches degree b+n-2, with coefficient 2bn. A separately coded distance-two independent-set enumeration agrees for eleven profiles, and literal shortest-path testing agrees for every subset on 8- and 12-vertex boundaries. These computations are not treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2023 Hamming theorem establishes the distance-two characterization and scalar maximum, not the full cardinality polynomial. The 2024 work introduces visibility polynomials generally and supplies unrelated exact families; it does not state this product formula. The already known binary--binary-factor enumeration is explicitly excluded from the originality claim. A fresh disjoint-support enumeration is needed for independently variable b,n>=3; no equivalent full formula was identified in the inspected sources or focused searches. Publication priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: An equivalent all-subset count may be published as an independence polynomial of a Hamming exact-distance-two graph or as a constrained code enumerator.
The already known binary--binary-factor case gives an overlapping boundary identity, explicitly not part of the new claim.
No independent audit or exhaustive literature-corpus verification has been performed.

value.rationale: A published natural extremal Hamming visibility problem is refined to a complete two-parameter counting formula, with a structural partition of all feasible sets and the exact 2bn optimizer multiplicity for b,n>=3. This answers natural coefficient and maximum-set enumeration questions for graph products and forbidden-distance codes; it is not a chosen isolated parameter value or a routine restatement of the known b=2 boundary.
